newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila court stops tariff cut on farm products.
newsitem.headline: Manila court stops tariff cut on farm products.

text.p: A Philippine court has stopped the government from allowing imports of agricultural products at lower tariff rates, documents released by the Manila Regional Trial Court on Wednesday said.

The court, in a ruling on June 5, restrained Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero from implementing an order issued in 1996 setting regulations on the minimum volume of annual farm imports at lower tariff as part of Manila's commitment to the World Trade Organisation.

The court order will affect additional imports on corn, sugar, beef, pork, and chicken under the minimum access volume (MAV) scheme, National Food Authority (NFA) deputy administrator Gregorio Tan said.
The Philippine Federation of Food Industries Inc had asked for the scrapping of the MAV scheme because it discriminates against new players in the business, court documents said.
The government issues import licenses under MAV only to existing producers, processors and traders of agriculture products.
Traders told Reuters the court order would affect proposals to import at least 300,000 tonnes of corn and between 300,000 and 350,000 tonnes of sugar under the MAV.
